messages.text: Remarkable Razaullah knock denies England series sweep inside three days

metadata.summary: England were denied a series sweep of Pakistan inside three days of the final Test at Edgbaston after a remarkable display of six-hitting from 21-year-old Razaullah late on Friday.
metadata.content: England vs Pakistan: Razaullah, 21, hits remarkable 81 off 63 balls featuring nine sixes to force final Test into fourth day | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content England vs Pakistan: Razaullah, 21, hits remarkable 81 off 63 balls featuring nine sixes to force final Test into fourth day Dan Lawrence dismisses Razaullah (81 off 63 balls) with what proves to be the last ball of day three; Pakistan all out for 449 after battling second innings; England set 130 to win on day four - watch live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15am, Saturday By David Currie at Edgbaston Friday 11 September 2026 19:33, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Razaullah smashed nine sixes to equal Tim Southee’s record for the most by a player on Test debut during a remarkable innings against England at Edgbaston. England were denied a series sweep of Pakistan inside three days of the final Test at Edgbaston after a remarkable display of six-hitting from 21-year-old Razaullah late on Friday. Pakistan enjoyed easily their finest day of what's otherwise been a dismal series but were still trailing by two when their eighth wicket fell early into the evening session, only for Razaullah to smash 81 off just 63 deliveries, clearing the ropes a staggering nine times to equal Tim Southee's record for a debutant. metadata.summary: Durham clinched promotion to Division One of the Rothesay County Championship with a 93-run victory over Middlesex at Chester-le-Street.
metadata.content: County Championship: Ben Stokes back in top flight as Durham promoted after victory over Middlesex | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content County Championship: Ben Stokes back in top flight as Durham promoted after victory over Middlesex Durham complete return to domestic cricket's top flight by beating Middlesex with Callum Parkinson and Brydon Carse claiming four wickets apiece; Olly Stone took five as Nottinghamshire beat Hampshire and JT Langridge did likewise as Gloucestershire beat Lancashire Stuart Hodge @Hodgeythehack Friday 11 September 2026 17:32, UK Image: Brydon Carse (left) and Ben Stokes (right) in County Championship cricket action for Durham (PA Images) Durham clinched promotion to Division One of the Rothesay County Championship with a 93-run victory over Middlesex at Chester-le-Street. The north-east side began the final day needing eight wickets and Kasey Aldridge struck with the first ball to set the tone. Despite a battling unbeaten ton from Harry Duke alongside Ben Geddes' half-century, Durham took control with the ball as Callum Parkinson finished with four wickets for 45 runs and Brydon Carse also claimed four to secure their spot back in the top flight next year. messages.text: Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Doncaster Cup

metadata.summary: Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointing efforts at Royal Ascot and York to win the Betfred Howards Wright Doncaster Cup.
metadata.content: Doncaster Cup: George Scott's Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Town Moor Group 2 | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Doncaster Cup: George Scott's Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Town Moor Group 2 Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointment at York with a decisive victory in the Doncaster Cup; Also on the card, Final Objective got up in the final strides to deny Crownbreaker in the Flying Childers Stakes Friday 11 September 2026 15:54, UK Image: Caballo De Mar won the Doncaster Cup under Oisín Murphy Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointing efforts at Royal Ascot and York to win the Betfred Howards Wright Doncaster Cup. Questions had been raised over whether the five-year-old still had the stomach for the fight after coming home last in the Gold Cup and stopping quickly before finishing fourth in the Lonsdale Cup at York. But after taking up the running a furlong from home on Town Moor under Oisín Murphy, the George Scott-trained stayer proved his doubters wrong, pulling away from Beylerbeyi to land odds of 5-6 favourite by a length and a quarter. The race had been robbed of its likely favourite after Queenstown was pulled out and there was also drama beforehand when the Emmet Mullins-trained Winday gave trouble at the start. Having worked himself up into a sweat, he failed to the fire in the race itself, finishing a tailed off last of seven. messages.text: Celtic given 'general behaviour' message by police ahead of Old Firm clash

metadata.summary: Martin O'Neill revealed Celtic were given a "general behaviour" warning by Police Scotland ahead of Sunday's League Cup quarter-final against Rangers at Ibrox.
metadata.content: Rangers vs Celtic: Martin O'Neill reveals 'general behaviour' message from police ahead of Old Firm League Cup clash | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Rangers vs Celtic: Martin O'Neill reveals 'general behaviour' message from police ahead of Old Firm League Cup clash Celtic face Rangers at Ibrox in Sunday's League Cup quarter-final; there will be no away fans after SPFL ruling; Mika Baur is available for the Hoops despite missing training; Martin O'Neill's side have won all six of their Premiership games this season Friday 11 September 2026 15:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic manager Martin O'Neill admits it will be strange to face Rangers at Ibrox with no away fans after the SPFL imposed a ban Martin O'Neill revealed Celtic were given a "general behaviour" warning by Police Scotland ahead of Sunday's League Cup quarter-final against Rangers at Ibrox. There will be no Hoops fans in the 50,000-capacity stadium at the order of the authorities amid a ticket allocation spat between the two Glasgow giants. The spat is partly a result of the last Old Firm clash in Govan in March, which was marred by fans' disorder as Celtic won the Scottish Gas Scottish Cup quarter-final on penalties after a goalless 120 minutes. messages.text: Late Ciganda magic keeps Europe locked with USA at Solheim Cup

metadata.summary: Carlota Ciganda delivered final-hole magic for Team Europe to leave them tied 4-4 with Team USA after a dramatic opening day at the Solheim Cup, where Charley Hull and Lottie Woad let a big lead slip as Team Europe’s star pair.
metadata.content: Solheim Cup 2026: Team Europe and Team USA tied 4-4 after tight opening day and Carlota Ciganda's dramatic finish | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Solheim Cup 2026: Team Europe and Team USA tied 4-4 after tight opening day and Carlota Ciganda's dramatic finish Team Europe and Team USA are tied after the opening day for just the second time in Solheim Cup history; Carlota Ciganda's late par-save ensured both teams claimed two points in both sessions at Bernardus Golf; watch day two live on Saturday from 6am on Sky Sports Golf By Ali Stafford at Bernardus Golf Friday 11 September 2026 19:20, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Friday fourballs from the Solheim Cup at Bernardus Golf, in the Netherlands Carlota Ciganda delivered final-hole magic for Team Europe to leave them tied 4-4 with Team USA after a dramatic opening day at the Solheim Cup, where Charley Hull and Lottie Woad let a big lead slip as Team Europe’s star pair. Both teams claimed a share of the spoils in the morning foursomes before producing a repeat result in the afternoon session, as Angela Stanford's American side looked set to hold an opening-day lead until Ciganda's impressive finish. Ciganda nailed a 15-foot par-save with the final shot of a thrilling day at Bernardus Golf, seeing her and rookie Julia Lopez Ramirez scramble a half-point against world No 1 Nelly Korda and Lauren Coughlin.
